Hirebotics brings iPhone spatial teaching to Cobot Painter

Smart Teach records phone positions and orientations so Beacon can generate editable painting paths.

RoboticsTomorrow ↗22 October 2026English editorial summary
StoryVideos 1

Teaching around the physical workpiece

Hirebotics introduced updated Smart Teach at FABTECH on October 22. Operators move an iPhone around a part and capture positions and orientations, allowing Beacon to generate a paint path without code or a CAD model. This supplements physically guiding a cobot through individual points.

Reaching awkward surfaces

A small phone can capture points behind, beside or inside large and complex parts more easily than moving the full robot arm. Operators can review generated paths and adjust points, spray parameters and other settings. Programs still need application review rather than automatic acceptance of coating quality.

Painting first, other processes later

Cobot Painter is the first target, with the required iPhone supplied with the system. Cobot Welder and Cobot Cutter are future expansion plans. No measured teaching-time comparison or supported-phone list was provided. The article mentions a video but supplies no clip URL.
